I have farmed for a long time on a small piece of land, so I will keep this year’s plan steady and manageable. I am 68, my household labor is limited, and I have only 5.0 mu, so I will not spread myself too thin or chase risky high-input production. I will keep the land divided among the crops I already know well, with a little more area in cabbage because it fits my usual system and gives me solid output, while maize stays in the plan because it is stable and less troublesome. I have well irrigation, so I will use water to keep the crops from stressing, but I will not over-irrigate because that raises cost and can bring disease. I will use hybrids for cabbage and chili because I want stronger uniformity and yield, improved seed for maize and kidney bean because they are reliable and easier for me to manage, and I will keep spinach simple but productive. I will use moderate fertilizer rates instead of pushing too hard, because on my farm stable yield matters more than maximum yield. I will also keep tillage practical: rotary tillage for most vegetable land because it is easier on a small farm, and ploughing for maize where I want a firmer field setup. I will spray when needed to protect the crop, but I will keep the number of applications controlled because every extra pass costs labor and money.
